accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 48, printed 34, lines 14-17 states the Fortran 2008 compatibility baseline and exception boundary.
Except for identified incompatibilities and deleted features, this document is an upward-compatible extension to Fortran 2008.
Deleted features noted in Clause B.2 are excluded from the compatibility statement; this overview exclusion does not itself own Annex B or current numbered-rule treatment.
A standard-conforming Fortran 2008 program remains conforming only if it avoids deleted features and features identified here as no longer permitted.

PDF 48 lines 18-21 contrasts the Fortran 2008 FLUSH IOSTAT rule with the current unsupported-FLUSH status rule. The current distinctness obligation is cross-referenced to existing owner doc/catalogues/iostat_specifier_12_11_5.json S12.11.5-006; the local compatibility paragraph owns no duplicate S facet.
The first sentence reports the former Fortran 2008 rule for unsupported FLUSH operations.
The current unsupported-FLUSH value remains processor dependent and negative; exact numeric values are not portable oracles.
Unsupported FLUSH status is distinct from IOSTAT_EOR and IOSTAT_END; existing owner doc/catalogues/iostat_specifier_12_11_5.json S12.11.5-006 covers this rule.

PDF 48 lines 22-25 summarizes a DO CONCURRENT incompatibility involving noncontiguous actual arguments and contiguous INTENT(INOUT) dummies. Existing owner doc/catalogues/additional_semantics_for_do_concurrent_constructs_11_1_7_5.json covers the SHARED and unspecified-locality noncontiguous contiguous-INTENT(INOUT) obligations in S11.1.7.5-010 and S11.1.7.5-011.

The described cross-iteration definition pattern is no longer permitted; existing owner doc/catalogues/additional_semantics_for_do_concurrent_constructs_11_1_7_5.json covers it through p6.shared-noncontiguous-contiguous-inout-rule and p7.unspecified-noncontiguous-dummy-rule.

PDF 48 lines 26-28 summarizes volatile restrictions for pure procedures and statement functions. Existing owner doc/catalogues/pure_procedures_15_7.json covers the statement-function VOLATILE condition, pure local/BLOCK VOLATILE exclusions, and pure volatile-designator prohibition.
A pure statement function may no longer reference a volatile variable; existing owner doc/catalogues/pure_procedures_15_7.json covers this in S15.7-001 and the pure volatile-designator restriction.

A local variable of a pure subprogram, or of a BLOCK construct within a pure subprogram, may no longer be volatile merely because it is unused; existing owner doc/catalogues/pure_procedures_15_7.json C1598 covers pure local and block variables not having VOLATILE.

PDF 48 lines 29-30 summarizes a pure-function result restriction. Existing owner doc/catalogues/pure_procedures_15_7.json C1594 covers polymorphic allocatable pure function results and polymorphic allocatable ultimate components.
A pure function result may no longer have a polymorphic allocatable ultimate component; existing owner doc/catalogues/pure_procedures_15_7.json C1594 covers this restriction.

PDF 48 lines 31-32 summarizes a PROTECTED TARGET initial-data-target incompatibility. Existing owner doc/catalogues/protected_attribute_8_5_15.json C859 includes the initial-data-target prohibition for use-associated protected nonpointers; doc/catalogues/initialization_8_4.json covers initial-data-target effects.

A PROTECTED TARGET variable accessed by use association may no longer be used as an initial-data-target; existing owner doc/catalogues/protected_attribute_8_5_15.json C859.initial-data-target covers this restriction.

PDF 48 lines 33-35 summarizes LOCK_TYPE named-constant restrictions. Existing owner doc/catalogues/lock_type_16_10_2_19.json C1607-C1608 covers LOCK_TYPE named-entity/component categories and coarray requirements.
A named constant may no longer have declared type LOCK_TYPE; existing owner doc/catalogues/lock_type_16_10_2_19.json C1607 requires the named entity to be a variable, excluding a named constant.

A named constant may no longer have a noncoarray potential subobject component with declared type LOCK_TYPE; existing owner doc/catalogues/lock_type_16_10_2_19.json C1607-C1608 covers the variable/coarray requirements for such LOCK_TYPE subobjects.

PDF 48 lines 36-37 summarizes a DO CONCURRENT finalization incompatibility. Existing owner doc/catalogues/additional_semantics_for_do_concurrent_constructs_11_1_7_5.json C1144 covers statements that might deallocate polymorphic entities within DO CONCURRENT constructs.

A polymorphic object may no longer be finalized within a DO CONCURRENT construct; existing owner doc/catalogues/additional_semantics_for_do_concurrent_constructs_11_1_7_5.json C1144 covers the operative prohibition through statements that might deallocate polymorphic entities.

PDF 48 lines 38-41 summarizes assignment allocation restrictions for unallocated allocatable coarrays or coindexed objects. Existing owner doc/catalogues/intrinsic_assignment_statement_10_2_1_2.json S10.2.1.2-011 covers coarray/coindexed intrinsic-assignment variables not being unallocated allocatables; runtime coarray/image evidence remains outside this packet.

Assignment may no longer allocate an unallocated allocatable coarray or coindexed object under the former scalar, nonpolymorphic, no-deferred-parameter conditions; existing owner doc/catalogues/intrinsic_assignment_statement_10_2_1_2.json S10.2.1.2-011 covers this restriction.

PDF 48 lines 42-43 contrasts a former RANDOM_NUMBER generator latitude with the current separate-seed rule. The former common-generator statement is permission/latitude; existing owner doc/catalogues/random_seed_16_9_169.json S16.9.169-006 covers invoking-image seed isolation.
The first sentence reports the former Fortran 2008 permission to use a common pseudorandom number generator for all images.

The current document requires separate seeds on each image; existing owner doc/catalogues/random_seed_16_9_169.json S16.9.169-006 covers invoking-image-only seed effects, and multi-image runtime facets are outside this packet.

PDF 48 lines 44-45 contrasts the Fortran 2008 ACOSH complex-result rule with the current rule. Existing owner doc/catalogues/acosh_intrinsic_16_9_6.json S16.9.6-004 covers complex ACOSH result range constraints.
The first sentence reports the former Fortran 2008 ACOSH rule for the imaginary part.

The current ACOSH result for a complex value must have a nonnegative real part and has no corresponding requirement on the imaginary part; existing owner doc/catalogues/acosh_intrinsic_16_9_6.json S16.9.6-004 covers the nonnegative real part and range constraints.

PDF 49 lines 1-4 repeats the SYSTEM_CLOCK argument restrictions also listed for Fortran 2018 compatibility. Existing owner doc/catalogues/system_clock_16_9_202.json S16.9.202-001 covers the decimal exponent range and same-kind argument restrictions.
Integer SYSTEM_CLOCK arguments now need decimal exponent range at least as large as a default integer; existing owner doc/catalogues/system_clock_16_9_202.json S16.9.202-001 covers this restriction.
All integer arguments in one SYSTEM_CLOCK reference now need the same kind type parameter; existing owner doc/catalogues/system_clock_16_9_202.json S16.9.202-001 covers this restriction.

PDF 49 lines 5-6 repeats the DATA-before-use restriction for BLOCK construct entities also listed for Fortran 2018 compatibility; existing owner doc/catalogues/statement_and_construct_entities_19_4.json S19.4-004 covers the rule.

A construct entity declared only by DATA initialization shall not be used before that DATA statement; existing owner doc/catalogues/statement_and_construct_entities_19_4.json S19.4-004 covers this restriction.

PDF 49 lines 7-8 repeats the ASSOCIATED rank incompatibility also listed for Fortran 2018 compatibility. Existing owner doc/catalogues/associated_intrinsic_16_9_20.json S16.9.20-007 covers non-assumed-rank POINTER/TARGET same rank.
POINTER and TARGET arguments to ASSOCIATED may no longer have different rank; existing owner doc/catalogues/associated_intrinsic_16_9_20.json S16.9.20-007 covers this restriction.

PDF 49 lines 9-16 lists Fortran 2008 features that might have a different interpretation. The bullets are compatibility notices with exact existing owners named on their fine units, not new local facets.

Deferred-length allocatable character assignment by IOMSG=, ERRMSG=, internal WRITE unit usage, or intrinsic subroutine INTENT(OUT) now follows intrinsic assignment semantics. Existing main owners confirmed: doc/catalogues/assignment.json section 10.2.1.3, doc/catalogues/iomsg_specifier_12_11_6.json, doc/catalogues/errmsg_specifier_9_7_5.json, and doc/catalogues/internal_files_12_4.json S12.4-007.

The document permits SYSTEM_CLOCK to use two or more clocks with characteristics based on argument type and kind; existing owner doc/catalogues/system_clock_16_9_202.json covers this latitude in S16.9.202-008 and clock selection in S16.9.202-009.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clauses 1 and 2 and the compatibility subclauses 4.3-4.3.4 (batch246). Scope and normative-reference text is structural; compatibility statements that restate rules owned elsewhere cross-reference their owners (12.11.5, 19.4, C1598) instead of duplicating them. Source accounting only.
